answer_1.quote: We present a hybrid approach for dialogical data collection, which combines the intervention of human expert annotators over machine generated dialogues ... The result of this work is DIALOCONAN, the first dataset comprising over 3000 fictitious multi‑turn dialogues between a hater and an NGO operator.
answer_1.outputs: Multi‑turn dialogues containing hateful speech (HS) and counter‑narratives (CN) generated by LM configurations and post‑edited by human annotators.

answer_2.quote: We use several metrics to assess the performance of each strategy. These metrics are aimed to assess either the efficiency of the procedure or the quality of the obtained data. HTER is an efficiency metric ... Turn deletion is the percentage of turns that are discarded ... Turn swap is the percentage of turns that are moved ... Novelty is utilized to check the quality of a generated dialogue by measuring its lexical difference ... Repetition Rate (RR) measures the language diversity within a corpus ...

answer_4.quote: Three annotators were recruited from a pool of internship students. They have been extensively trained ... The annotators should keep the gold HS as it is, while post‑editing the most promising among the 3 CN paraphrasis suggestions ... The annotators should check the veracity of fact‑based statements since they might derive from LM hallucinations.
answer_4.guideline: Post‑editing instructions: keep HS unchanged, edit CN for naturalness and novelty, avoid turn swaps/deletions in Session 2, verify factual statements, minimize intervention while ensuring dialogue flow.
